why: Carrying the disc over from the prior beat preserves identity through the blackout, and scaling in a dense interface lets the viewer accept it before reading.

title: Headline number blooms into an integrations mosaic
why: Showing the figure fully formed, with no ticking counter, conveys magnitude instantly, and the grainy mosaic links it to the film's recurring data-harvesting look.

title: Provider handoff settles into the closing wordmark
why: A directional handoff places the product between the viewer and their model options, and one dimmed logo implies others without promising a partnership.

title: Opening question becomes the product's name
why: Words arriving on separate beats make the line sound addressed to the viewer, and the automatic resize suggests the sentence is still taking shape.

title: Mascot and style samples flow into the composer
why: The logo's visual pun is read in one go, then growth itself carries the viewer into the next act, so no cut is needed.

title: Completing the prompt and passing control to the viewer
why: Real-time typing feels like a person writing, and the sudden size snap turns a spilling thought into a committed sentence that fits the frame.

title: Headline lands while a product is edited live
why: The claim is read word by word, as if being written live, and the accent hue picks out the key part without needing another graphic.

title: A figure becomes a mechanism, then a physical comparison
why: A moving number grabs attention, then lands on a tidy round figure, so the viewer feels the amount settle instead of merely reading it.

title: A real device leads to integration breadth
why: A phone showing live figures looks like a shipped app instead of a concept board, giving the viewer something tangible to picture holding.

title: Token choices turn into a typed request
why: A breadth statistic becomes a countable object: watching the inventory expand is more convincing than trusting a digit.

title: Mascot personality, then a tactile money metaphor
why: A playful character beat followed by a reveal: the viewer smiles at the jump, then is shown the larger system the product sits in.

title: Claim transforms into a polished product surface
why: The sentence shrinks into a portable badge: words dissolve while their icons persist as a single object, so the claim finishes as a symbol.

title: Cursor nears the call to action; brand held
why: The button glows, the cursor closes in, and the cut lands before the press, handing the final click to the viewer.

title: Blueprint flash, written claim, graphic handoff
why: A flash of technical drawing says this brand is built with care before any text appears, so craft registers subconsciously rather than being read.

title: Parameter system shown in several visual modes
why: One rig showing six clearly different behaviours suggests the brand works as a system with adjustable controls on every axis.

title: Claim assembled, scaled up, then laid out
why: Feeding one word per beat sets a spoken cadence, so the claim registers like speech instead of a paragraph to skim.

title: Brand reveal turns into the product's action
why: The name is stamped, not faded, at the energy peak right after the problem section, so attribution lands as the payoff.

title: Inputs gather into knowledge, then the payoff line
why: Scattered inputs merge into one dense shape, so learning is demonstrated visually before the sentence ever claims it.

title: Opening claim and range define the visual system
why: Each word arrives as its own beat, all stamped by one accent hue, so the headline is heard like a list instead of a block of text.

title: Camera pulls back into the brand lockup
why: Starting nose-to-glass on a single word and then easing out to open space makes the name that follows land as the answer.

title: Stating the promise and sending a prompt
why: Because the sentence recenters while it grows, it feels composed live instead of read from a finished card, and pairing two lines turns a claim into a demo.

title: Opening identity swap
why: A name is overwritten in place, so old and new identities both register from one static lockup without a cut, and the accent tint comes to mean incoming text.

title: Entering the product, typing, and sending
why: A close-up of the logo detail carries the viewer straight into the interface, so the product feels housed in the brand mark and not a separate scene.

rule: WHEN the UI is the proof (checklist, prompt, modal) -> DO NOT show the app. Crop to ONE object at 3.3x (card 0.76W x 0.44H, text 36 px = 0.05H) and reveal the product only by pulling back. BECAUSE the viewer reads one thing at a time and the pull-back becomes the "oh, it was inside a real product" beat. (M913, M919 x4.39, M918 1.42x, M916 1.5x)

WHEN a camera move reveals or reframes -> DO one-frame snaps (scale ratio 0.56-0.77 in 1 frame: M913 2.50 -> 1.41 at 3.12-3.16; M914 1.469 -> 1.137 at 2.84-2.88) followed by a 0.3-0.6 s decelerating tail; never one global ease. BECAUSE the jump has a punch the eye feels as a cut, and the tail lets it read. (M913, M914, M917, M918)

WHEN any object enters -> DO decelerate: about 60-72% of the travel in the first 4 frames (0.13-0.16 s), then a 0.4-0.6 s tail, no overshoot (card 0.76W: 0.26 -> 0.12; M914 862 -> 576: 72% by 0.16 s; M916 card: 62% by 0.13 s). BECAUSE it reads as heavy and certain, not bouncy. (M913, M914, M916, M919)

WHEN anything leaves -> DO accelerate (ease-in) over 6-10 frames and exit off-frame, 17 -> 111 px/frame (M920), button edge 0.37 -> -0.16 in 5 frames with smear 20 -> 140 px (M919), card y 0.36 -> 0.27 accelerating (M914), pan ends still accelerating (M913). BECAUSE the object is "thrown away", clearing the frame for the next idea with no wasted dead frames. (M913, M914, M919, M920)

WHEN a task list shows progress -> DO state machine: pending = white + dashed ring; active = dim grey (#808086) + spinner; done = white + check; swap icon in ONE frame with a 14-18 px sideways nudge returning over 6-8 frames, no scale bounce; start the next row's dim/spinner-grow 0.04-0.12 s BEFORE the previous check; about 0.9 s per row. BECAUSE it shows labour in discrete, believable steps and the list never idles. (M913)
WHEN the result of a tool/agent step lands -> DO let completion release the camera (M913: last check 2.72, snap 3.12). BECAUSE cause -> effect is read as "the work finished, so the product appeared".

WHEN text types in a UI -> DO per grapheme at about 3.4 chars/frame (about 85 chars/s; 67-68 chars in 0.8 s), caret appears 0.04 s before the first char and follows the last glyph, leading 1-2 glyphs brighter and faintly ghosted, blink windows after typing; prompt sized about 0.04-0.05H; zoom the camera in steps while it types so the target is already bigger. BECAUSE it is fast enough to not bore and slow enough to be recognised as typing. (M914, M919)

WHEN a cursor must "click" -> DO one persistent top-layer cursor with a curved path (heading rotating with travel), arrive and PARK 0.16-0.5 s on the target while the camera zooms onto it, THEN press: cursor squash to 0.71-0.9 over 2 frames, button reacts 0-1 frame later (0.63-0.80 min), rebound +5% (1.055), then rings 0.48 s starting on the press frame (M914). BECAUSE the park gives the viewer time to find the target, and cause -> effect order makes the click feel real. (M914, M919)

WHEN you animate a cursor -> DO never swap to hand/I-beam; the cursor's size follows the camera scale; its 3D "edge-on" turn is rotateY to 45% width, not a sprite swap; exits by acceleration (0.04W/frame) or shrinks to zero in place (M918, 0.29 s). BECAUSE cursor continuity keeps the "real recording" illusion.

WHEN a status/log line shows machine work -> DO per-word blur-in (12 px blur / 0.1 opacity -> sharp in 4 frames, words back-to-back), then show "thinking" with a shimmer: a masked brighter copy of the grey text, band about 0.23W, two passes of 0.42 s with a 0.21 s gap; leave by an L->R wipe 0.16 s and replace with a green check drawn on 0.08 s. BECAUSE nothing "types" for the agent and it looks like inference.

WHEN a persistent character (mascot) exists -> DO use ONE instance as the agent's marker: sweep in with 25 px smear, decelerate, scale with the camera, drop straight down while the check stays behind (smear about 100 px), shrink about a fixed centre at the end (0.14W -> 0.06W in 0.6 s). Never fly in from above or bounce. (M919, M920, M916, M917) BECAUSE the viewer tracks the agent's "position in the job".

WHEN a light->dark or scale change would otherwise look like a jump -> DO hide it in a 4-frame flat dip (30% -> 65% -> ONE flat #7D7D7D frame -> clear by 1.42) and carry the action across (pill slide continues; rail 1.5x magnified, labels 0.05H -> 0.07H). BECAUSE the cut feels like motion continuing, and the flip signals "now it's the AI part" without copy. (M916)

WHEN a hard cut ends a move -> DO cut mid-motion (M916 whip at 2.79 mid-smear 65 px; M914 new scene already travelling at 1.84; M918 modal at 1.42x), leave 3 empty frames, and let the next object enter along the same vector ("meet" drifts up-left after the up-left whip). BECAUSE direction carries the eye across the cut.

WHEN words arrive as kinetic type -> DO whole words, each starts 0.03W right (+35, +12, +4, 0 px over 3 frames) with 24-30 px horizontal smear on frame 1, 2-3 frame gaps (0.08-0.12 s) between words, row drifts left 1.1-1.5 px/frame while held; phrase 1 -> 2 is a hard cut, not a fade; fade only the last phrase (linear, 10 frames) when you need black. BECAUSE it has the speech cadence of voice-over and no moment is static. (M920, M917, M918)

WHEN a line is replaced -> DO word-level handoff: drop the leading words in single frames (0.84, 0.88) without re-centring the survivors, then add the new words at the right (0.92, 1.08, 1.24). Never re-centre. BECAUSE it reads as backspace-and-retype, the metaphor for prompting. (M914)

WHEN a word changes identity (one word -> the product name) -> DO per-letter swap in 5 frames (3.42, 3.46, 3.54, 3.63), each letter blurs-and-drops 0.03H first and the new glyph arrives with the roll; never swap the whole word. BECAUSE the mechanism is visible, so the morph feels "built".

WHEN many items appear (13 tiles) -> DO one per frame (1 frame apart) scaling 0 -> 1.12 -> 1.0 in place, 3-4 px blur that clears in 0.33 s, no slide, total cascade about 0.5 s; match onsets to visual size. BECAUSE it reads as a data burst and "volume of work", not a fan-in.

WHEN the next scene is meant to feel continuous -> DO keep one anchor object across the cut (M918 -> M919: headline at 0.74W, 0.11H over a blurred backdrop; M914 -> M913: empty #0B0B0B card with #262627-#292929 border; M919 -> M920: grey status line + green check + a card with video). BECAUSE separately-cut moments feel like one take.

WHEN the UI must be backdrop for type -> DO rack-focus the UI, not the type: UI blur 0.7 -> 5.5 -> 10 -> 11 px over 0.7 s with 0.1 darkening while the headline words (4 frames apart) build at 1.39x -> 1.0x and stay crisp; cap the blur at about 11 px. BECAUSE text stays legible and the backdrop still reads as the proof. (M918)

WHEN you finish -> DO end mid-motion, no fade, no freeze: M913 pans still accelerating, M914 jumps to a new card, M916 lockup contracts 4.00-4.79 to 0.88, M917 shrinks, M920 sweeps cut off at 5.38. BECAUSE the cut is the edit and the silence feels earned.

WHEN a CTA/close is built -> DO build outward from the character: one-frame black (3.21), the character appears at max size (0.14W) and shrinks about its centre to 0.06W by 3.9 (decelerating); a 1 px line grows in alternating steps 12 -> 265 px (0.5 s), unsquashes in 8 discrete vertical steps (0.33 s) into a hollow 1 px outline, holds 0.12 s, goes SOLID in one frame; the CTA words focus in place (0.12 -> 1 opacity, 8 -> 0 px blur, 4 frames each, the CTA words back-to-back) so it is sharp 0.05 s after the logo goes solid; then a pink band sweep (about 130 px, 55 px/frame, period 0.708 s) and 1-frame top-half shear glitches (5 px, 12 px). Lockup 0.30W x 0.20H centred, 95% empty. Hold about 1.0 s resolved. (M920)

WHEN you spend colour -> DO neutral greys + ONE hue, used only for "the AI is acting" (typing, scan, sweep, shimmer, halo) and one separate signal (green) only for "done". Never use both on the same object at once. (M913, M914, M916, M919, M920) BECAUSE hue becomes meaning.

WHEN you pick a motion grammar -> DO pick one per film: Film A = crisp hard steps, no blur (M913, M914); Film B = directional smear along the travel vector (1-6 frames, 3 -> 65 px) + blur on every fast move (M916-M920). Do not mix per scene. BECAUSE grammar is a sign of authorship.

WHEN a demo needs an "output" feel -> DO let live footage play inside the card the whole time and use a warm bloom (yellow #ffee00 / orange #ff5a00, 20 px) or neon flash (decays by 0.33 s) on the card, with metrics static (no count-up). BECAUSE static thumbnails read as slides; moving thumbnails read as real outputs. (M917, M919, M920)

WHEN a scene should never be read as "a slide" -> DO ensure at least one element is moving at every frame: dot grid drift (0.02W over 2.9 s), rim highlight orbiting, never-freeze scale 0.88-0.90 (M916 4.00-4.79; M917 4.88-6.08; M918 3.04-4.54), scrubber creep, caret, row drift 1.1-1.5 px/frame. BECAUSE "holds" are alive.

WHEN a headline is built word by word -> DO make each word a 1-frame hard cut (or whole-word entry), 6-7 f apart at 60 fps (0.10-0.12 s), 10 f before the payoff word, then hold the assembled line ~0.9 s BECAUSE each landing reads as a stated fact and the longer gap before the key word is the emphasis. (M921)

WHEN a phrase is on screen -> DO keep a continuous slow drift along one axis (here -88 px = 6.9% W over 1.1 s, ~1.3 px/f) and accelerate the drift 7 -> 14 px/f in the last 2 frames before the cut BECAUSE a held line reads as a slide; the lean-out makes the cut feel pulled. (M921, M929)

WHEN a new word is added to a centred phrase -> DO land it with +12 to +32 px extra gap that closes ~50% in 7 f and finishes over 0.4-0.6 s, re-centring the phrase each time BECAUSE the line breathes and each word gets its own impact. (M921)

WHEN words rise into a line -> DO use an exponential ease-out (59% of 173 px = 24% H in 5 f at 30 fps, 91% by 16 f, tail ~1.2 s), start offsets that shrink per word (24/18/13/13% H), and let each word's tail overlap the next entrance BECAUSE the fast head gives energy, the long tail keeps the line alive, and shrinking travel makes the build accelerate toward the last word. (M929)

WHEN an entry needs smear -> DO put a vertical (or horizontal for lateral entries) kernel on frame 0-1 only (10-20 px -> 4 -> 2 -> 0 in 3 f) plus 1-2 px gaussian over 6 f; RGB split only on the FIRST word, 1-9 f; flat coloured rectangles stepping every 2 f instead of a tweened glitch BECAUSE the effect reads as speed, not decoration, and is spent where it matters. (M929)

WHEN the second phrase must feel like a reply -> DO change the axis: first phrase rises, second slides in horizontally from the right with 3 f of anticipation drift opposite to travel (+196 -> +234 px) then accelerate (peak 3.2% W/f) and a ~1 s settle; the follower word enters ~12 f later and catches up with a ~4 f half-life BECAUSE different verbs of motion separate ideas without a transition. (M929)

WHEN you hand off between scenes -> DO make the last frame of A equal the first frame of B in content, position and colour (carry text, ground, object) and begin B mid-motion BECAUSE the cut becomes invisible and the viewer reads one continuous thing. (M921->M922, M923->M924, M925->M926, M926->M927, M928->M929)

WHEN the ground must flip dark <-> light -> DO make the flip with a growing object (bead 0.04 -> 0.37 W in ~0.2 s, then a 0.58 W disk to 17x) or a 1-frame hard cut hidden in a sweeping band; never a white flash or crossfade BECAUSE the flip then has cause and direction. (M922, M924)

WHEN a UI scene opens -> DO keep the carried element (header, brand) fully lit at frame 0 and lift everything else from near-black over 0.3-1.0 s with a screen-blend colour wash sweep (not opacity fades) BECAUSE it says "the app was already running" and lights the UI like a product shot. (M922)

WHEN you simulate screen use -> DO move ONE parent camera (cut in at ~0.9 W crop with the lower half out of frame; pan ease-out ~0.020 -> 0.003 H/f; whip with peak 0.027 H/f; zoom) and never hold still BECAUSE continuous camera motion makes a 2D UI feel like a physical object. (M922)

WHEN a button is "pressed" -> DO squeeze about its centre to 0.76-0.80 (11-13 f down, ~19 f up at 60 fps) with a lighter fill (#4C4DF5 -> #7FA7F5); no overshoot, no ripple BECAUSE a clean squeeze reads as a deliberate tap. Add a hard cursor swap (arrow -> hand) 0.17 s before the click and shrink the hand to ~0.52 on the press. (M922, M928)

WHEN there is no pointer, give the eye a carrier: a shaded 0.04 W bead riding the device rim during the camera move, growing x1.5-2.2 per 3 f into the next scene BECAUSE it directs attention and gives the next scene a literal origin. (M922)

WHEN a control moves numbers -> DO ease-in-out every counter off one handle (expo-out zoom 1.69 -> 1.00 in 48 f; counters 69 -> 100% / $60 -> $193 in 50 f, update every frame, no overshoot) BECAUSE the viewer reads cause and effect without text. (M923)

WHEN morphing UI between two layouts -> DO only narrow/clip (slider pill width 0.53 -> 0.005 W in 36 f, constant height, handle clipped by the edge, ticks dying one by one) and grow the new layout around the caret as staggered fades with 3-5 px de-blur + 18-20 px upward settle, group onsets ~0.1 s apart BECAUSE clipping reads as physical, staggers keep the eye ordered. (M923)

WHEN something is typed -> DO match the data: 28-30 chars/s with irregular 1-f holds for human prompts (M928), right-aligned growth around a fixed caret for fields (M923), per-glyph colour sweeps (dim -> white) at 4 f then 2 f cadence for system text (M921); never blink a caret BECAUSE the cadence tells who is typing. (M921, M923, M927, M928)

WHEN using perspective -> DO use true perspective (track with horizon dropping as camera drops, label lying in the track plane, translucent hero object with blurred through-copy of the label), and give the hero a rise -> recede -> rush path with accelerating growth (5x faster in the last third), pinning its top edge BECAUSE it creates travel, not a scale-up. (M924)

WHEN the finale is a counter or a ring -> DO decelerate (3.1 pts/f -> 0.5 pts/f), park on 99 for 5 f, land 100 without a flash, and keep scaling the whole card (0.43 -> 0.89 W) through to the last frame BECAUSE the last 1% becomes suspense and the card feels like it keeps coming at you. (M924)

WHEN a question must turn into a brand -> DO make the brand mark the same object as the question's pointer: shapes collapse (cards round 3 -> 19% and shrink) into the mark, one 1-frame oversize pop at ~3x settled size (hard step 1.27, pop 1.30, settle by 1.67), mark slides left to lead the question, the question enters whole from the right (50% of travel in 2 f), then TWO independent soft masks erase the question and reveal the name in place (mint 25-45 px leading edge, erase front leading the reveal front, ~0.1 s gap) while the mark slides back right over the text as the name's tail BECAUSE the viewer's own answer is spent as the reveal, and nothing crossfades. (M926)

WHEN you build a CTA -> DO sequence tagline (1.7 s) -> second phrase (1.5 s) -> icon (0.8 s) -> wordmark, three hard cuts, the last into a dark ground; the icon only shrinks (accelerating 1.0 -> 0.70), the wordmark crashes from 3.75x with 96 stacked scaled copies as radial streaks (39% of the collapse in 1 f, 1.0x at 0.67 s) and keeps contracting with a slight flicker, accelerating again in the last 0.2 s, no fade, visible on the last frame; wordmark ink 0.28 W so empty space carries the glow BECAUSE the sign-off feels thrown at the viewer, then lingering. (M929)

WHEN showing 4 data surfaces in 4 s -> DO use one repeatable birth (1-frame slab, 25-30 px smear, grows to 0.5 H over ~0.47 s while darkening), ~0.75 s apart, one live micro-proof each (gauge to 77% of the arc, last digit rolls, waveform wipe), stack the previous card to a rear peek (left edge 0.50, 0.21 W) BECAUSE the repeat becomes a rhythm, the micro-proof proves it's live. (M927)

WHEN a state change happens to text -> DO use travelling soft-edged masks, not crossfades (M926 swap, M927 Limit row fades in as separate row while both rise 0.075 H) BECAUSE motion shows where it comes from.

WHEN one accent colour exists -> DO spend it on arrival flashes that decay to ink (ticker violet sweep -> white, "data" green -> ink, "making" mint 4-6 f -> white) and on one action (Close button) BECAUSE colour then marks the newest thing.

WHEN you need the ground to change mid-scene -> DO ramp it as one continuous straight-sRGB track over 0.5-0.7 s timed to what is leaving (cards -> teal, #ECEEEB -> #41977F) BECAUSE a cut/fade of the ground breaks the continuity of the objects.

WHEN a UI event is the point (switch, drop, click) → DO make the cause land first and the effect 1-2 frames after contact begins, flipping state in 2 frames (knob, one pale frame, full colour) with NO glow/ring; follow with the secondary cascade 5 frames later. BECAUSE the eye reads causality from the tiny gap and the sparse cleanliness lets the cascade carry the drama. (evidence: M933 master at 1.17-1.21 then rows from 1.42; M931 drop at 0.67)

WHEN one action propagates to a list ("authorize once, everyone") → DO a top-to-bottom cascade at 2-3 frames/item (0.08-0.12 s), 5-7 items, whole wave ≤0.6 s, uneven gaps (3,2,2,2,2,2) never uniform timer-looking. BECAUSE a wave short enough to hold in working memory reads as one gesture; too slow reads as a loading list. (M933, M935 gaps 3,3,2,2,2,4)

WHEN a wave crosses a 2D grid → DO origin-first, a convex front (centre rows lead outer rows by 3-6 f), ~5 f/column, items change on a 12 fps pose clock while the camera stays at 24-25 fps; orthogonal lattice with 5-10px jitter, never hex/random. BECAUSE the viewer sees "spreading" as geometry, and hand-posed items vs smooth camera gives craft without noise. (M934 WAVE table)

WHEN the camera whips between regions → DO 3-5 frames of travel: ease-in over ~10 frames (27% of travel), then 45-50% of travel in the 4 frames around the peak (~13% W per frame), then a 15-frame tail; add blur only if the film's language has blur (film A, C), otherwise change the content within the whip (panel/logo/lines exit with the pan). (M934, M931, M936)

WHEN you need an actual hard whip with a camera change → DO ramp blur+smear on the last 3 frames of the old view (text 8-20px, ~100px smear), cut with a one-frame discontinuity into a view that is ALREADY blurred (button as a smeared pill) and resolve over ~8 frames; swap scale at the cut (2x). BECAUSE both sides share blur so the cut is hidden and the arrival reads as inertia. (M931 1.53; M937 18px>80px)

WHEN you move a big card/panel as a "camera settle" → DO slow-in/fast-middle/long-tail: 27% of travel in the first 0.46 s, 42% in 3 frames, 25% in a 0.7 s tail, scale 1>0.6 simultaneously, no overshoot, never fully off screen (leave 0.20 W of its edge as an anchor). (M933 2.33-3.58)

WHEN highlighting a key word in a line → DO choose by metaphor: product-mechanic = hard-cut selection boxes (#354BAA solid, 4-5 frames each, one empty frame between boxes, text dims not inverts, one box per word, cut in AND out) fired the moment the line is complete; editorial = hand-drawn loop (5px stroke, 9 held 2-frame poses over 0.75 s, drawn from under an object, held ~0.7 s, exits as a NEW curl, still visible at the cut). Never both, never an underline/glow. BECAUSE the highlight must say which word is the claim without becoming an extra object. (M930, M933)

WHEN a hero number counts → DO one value per frame, with non-round steps (+8-9 each, 7 frames), the number growing 0.12>0.22 H while colour/blur resolve (grey, 5px blur > #5C sharp > black one beat after landing); hold solid 1.24 s; then fade its label up from blur 0.2 s after it lands. For 1..N counters: 1 frame (40 ms) per digit, growing ~12%/frame, last digit reaches size one beat later. BECAUSE a count that ends sharp in <0.3 s feels like impact; holds make it a fact. (M936)

WHEN comparing two quantities (30:00 vs 6 weeks) → DO render them at the same height (0.22 H), keep the sentence text small (0.067-0.08 H), reserve pure black for the figure and charcoal elsewhere, and never settle the second one (cropped at the edge mid-slide: 6 accelerates out -11,-12,-19,-30 px/f while "weeks" decelerates in -70,-62,-54). BECAUSE equal weight reads as a fair comparison; motion at the cut implies there is more. (M936)

WHEN removing/replacing words in a sequence → DO exit 1 frame apart (3-4 frames each, up 0.07 H + fade) and enter 2-5 frames apart from different offsets (0.07-0.22 H below) onto one baseline with exponential ease-out ~15 f; on the same pass overlap the exit with the next entrance by ~2 frames. BECAUSE exits are faster than entrances; overlap keeps reading momentum. (M938 0.00/0.12/0.20/0.32 in, 1.00/1.04/1.08/1.12 out)

WHEN a phrase needs word-by-word reading → DO whole words not letters: pop in 1 frame (or from 5px blur resolving in 4 f), offset right, each decelerating left on its own track (largest first step ~33px/f), colour ramping dark>grey for later words or grey>black in 4 stepped opacities (30/50/75/100), cadence 3-5 frames (accelerating 5,5,3,3), fixed slots, no re-centring. Typing only for UI text, left-anchored, 3-4 letters first. BECAUSE letter-typing makes titles look like a terminal; word-pops give rhythm that matches speech. (M936, M934, M937 "understand")

WHEN a logo grid appears → DO start oversized (2.5x, tiles are giant cropped squares), pull back in two surges (2.5>1.85 in 0.28 s, near-stall 0.28 s, >1.08 in 0.32 s, >0.875), tiles appear as outline glyph 1 frame apart (4 logos in 4 frames) then flip to filled in single frames in an uneven order (2,2,1 f), a late logo enters already filled from an edge as the pull-back reveals its cell, and pale filler cells pop (no fade) to make a lattice. The title sits in a 2x1 hole in the grid. BECAUSE the pull-back is the counting device: scale change gives a reveal rhythm with no extra elements. (M937)

WHEN the opening word is the thesis → DO make it enormous (0.91 W ink, 0.33 H), slow shrink 18% in 0.6 s, then accelerate (0.74>0.25 in 0.48 s) while blur ramps 0>18px and opacity 1>0.42, and hard-cut (no white frame) into the next defocused state. BECAUSE the viewer registers a thesis word before it leaves; the collapse is the transition. (M937)

WHEN an entry is a "reveal of identity" (hero title) → DO per-glyph blur-streak entrance (10>1px in 8 frames, ~1 glyph/frame, cold-blue>white in 0.3 s), a multi-phase path (glide, lift with 1-frame smear, jump with smear) to rest, additive glow dying by 0.5 s, and let the other words arrive by different mechanics (whole-word slide vs scattered glyph fragments). BECAUSE variety inside one line avoids the "typewriter title" look. (M930)

WHEN a title becomes a product shot → DO open a gap: insert a 0.03 thumbnail at the gap (wide 0.09x0.07), spread words (RGB split up to 9px, scale 0.06>0.09), HARD-CUT the title in 1 frame on the same frame the card box accelerates (35px of height/frame), and let a cover-fit video crop from wide to portrait (never stretched, always playing). BECAUSE the cut-on-motion makes the swap invisible. (M930)

WHEN dragging a card into a field → DO give the target a reaction stack: grow target 0.08 H, hover rim (#73C8F2) 0.4 s early, tilt card -8° at crest then 0° at drop, 2-frame crest hold, then ONE frame to attachment + cursor swap + flash, + a 0.2 s residual wash sliding off. Ground tint shifts 4% during the drag. BECAUSE one-frame snap with stacked feedback feels physical. (M931)

WHEN a cursor performs a click → DO: long decel in (first step 79px/f), hover 3-8 frames, swap art for press in 1 frame (or depress 0.03 H), recoil 0.92 over 3-5 frames, never ring/ripple on the cursor; put the click response in the UI (tint plate 0.25 opacity, button 0.81, no rebound); end the film ON the maximum compression. Pose changes (pointing>thumbs-up) are 1-frame swaps with an 8px bounce, no scale. BECAUSE cursor choreography is the product demo; hold-then-swap gives anticipation. (M930, M931, M933, M935)

WHEN you reveal a menu/popup → DO height-wipe (0.29>0.41 H in 4 frames) with rows fading in at 1-2 frame stagger, divider growing L>R, hover square behind the trigger appearing 0.17 s BEFORE the hand lands, popup 6 frames after landing; exit slides down while riding the zoom and fades only in the last 4 frames. BECAUSE staged reveal avoids a whole-panel fade. (M935)

WHEN many tokens must become instances → DO match-cut layout across clips (same lattice positions), let identical tokens morph into varied content at staggered 0.04-0.12 s offsets (inner pair first, outer last), with greeting text typed on, while the centre dot grows 0.01>0.9 W to become the next stage, contents on a separate scale track. BECAUSE continuity of position carries the eye through a hard cut. (M934>M935)

WHEN you stagger exits of physical objects → DO simulate bodies individually (own path, rotation, bounce 0.03 H, slight rotation overshoot -95>-90), settle by 1.8-2.2 s then HOLD 0.8-1.0 s motionless as the "weight" beat, then let the wash arrive; use ≥ one extra body entering late (0.60) to avoid choreographed uniformity. BECAUSE a group translation reads as a slide, individual bodies read as consequence. (M938)

WHEN washing a scene into a brand → DO a 0.28 H-feathered colour haze from the bottom (0.4 s rise), swell content 1.07>1.20x as it peaks, fade the objects bottom-first, then at the peak frame change to a pale gradient (never solid colour), build the mark bar by bar (1 per frame, gradient bars darkest-first right>left), the wordmark 1 glyph/frame with 5-frame grey>black fades and tracking collapsing +20>-3px while sliding left 0.11 W; keep shrinking the lockup (1>0.835 in 0.8 s, accelerating). BECAUSE the brand arrives as a resolution, and a shrinking lockup never feels pasted. (M938)

WHEN a CTA/sign-off follows a UI showcase → DO: (a) let the UI breathe (+3-8% in 0.3 s) then contract ease-in to 0.53x with 6px blur/12px smear into (b) localized glitch rectangles (3 rects, 6 frames, sparks #FF4E04 only in one) over a hard cut, (c) logo built from stems (7 frames, blue stem > cyan bloom r 0.06-0.09 > black one stem per 2 frames) with size matched to the contracting UI (0.16 W card to 0.11 W mark at the same centre), (d) never hold the mark (shrink 0.11>0.10 over 0.7 s then 0.07 in 0.16 s), (e) hard cut to the inverted ground and slam the name at 3.5x (1.7 W) with radial streaks (64 copies), 15px cyan/amber fringe, 65px bloom, resolved in ~5 frames (86% of the scale drop in 6 f), then keep creeping 1.0>0.57 over 1.2 s, glow in 3 layers (3/15/45px), ending mid-shrink with 7px zoom blur. BECAUSE the sign-off feels like arriving and leaving at once. (M932)

WHEN type has a weight/scale system → DO keep body at regular (350-500, sentence case, tracking -2.5 to -5% em on display), 6-9% H for statements, 22-33% H for hero figures, 14% H for wordmark (semibold only there), serif for emotional claim lines in the film where UI is sans. BECAUSE bold reads as template; scale contrast replaces weight contrast. (M930-M938)

WHEN holding a still moment → DO never freeze: keep slow shrink (0.82 per 0.6 s), 14°/s dial rotation, slow zoom (0.16 W badge growth over 3 s), a 0.5-0.8 s hold only with something alive (video, dial, drift). Where a true hold exists (M937 2.52-2.60, M931 hover 0.27 s, M938 0.8-1.0 s shape pile) it is pre-wipe. BECAUSE perfectly static frames read as slides. (M932, M936, M937, M931)

WHEN deciding how a clip ends → DO end on an action peak or mid-move (button at 0.81, "weeks" cropped and moving, wordmark mid-shrink, loop curl still visible, final frame hard cut to the next UI) and start the next clip with that momentum; reserve fades for individual objects (line 1 of a headline, 0.75>0.18 over 4 frames). BECAUSE the cut is a beat, not a pause. (M931, M932, M933, M936, M937, M938)

WHEN spending the accent → DO assign one semantic role per colour and spend it on ≤1 element per scene (single word "ideas", single loop, ON-state blue), with the glow colour matching only at events. BECAUSE accent loses power when diffused. (film A/B/C)

WHEN showing a long agent chat or log as proof of volume -> start at frame 0 fully populated and moving. Accelerate continuously from ~6 px/frame to ~250 px/frame (0.35 H/frame) over ~1.8 s. Use no blur, glow or stutter. Let the viewport run EMPTY (2.40) rather than invent filler. Decelerate over ~9 frames onto a short, large, readable list, then hold it still 0.8 s. BECAUSE the viewer reads speed and mass as competence, then gets one legible landing. (M939)

WHEN content passes too fast to read -> make blocks of distinct silhouette (table card, tall red/green diff card, green chips) at 9-14 px text. Keep ONE landmark ~.49 H tall. BECAUSE shapes keep rhythm when words cannot. (M939)

WHEN a new element joins a moving page -> pop it in whole as a step (task_complete card at 2.72, then ride the scroll). Never type, fade or slide it in. BECAUSE a step reads as a system event rather than an animation. (M939, M940)

WHEN wiping between two UI scenes -> use a feathered mask (.31-.42 of frame wide, 0.56-0.6 s) painted in the NEXT scene's ground colour. Start it 0.1-0.2 s before the voice line ends. Start the next hero (a vendor card, 6 px blur) 0.1 s before the wipe completes. Rotate direction across the film: R->L, B->T. BECAUSE overlap kills dead time and the wipe reveals rather than erases. (M939, M940)

WHEN the next scene is empty or one frame of UI -> hard cut (zero frames of fade) and let the new layout arrive already built, then move it (trace panel drops .09 H, decelerating, with the overlay clearing in 0.36 s). BECAUSE a cut with a built layout reads as app state, not as a transition. (M940, M941, M942)

WHEN stacking a list that pushes older items away -> insert the newest at the top as a blank tinted card, fill it 2-4 frames later, shove the stack in piecewise-linear jumps. First jump ~105 px in ONE frame, plus one real 2-frame hold. Add ~.02 W lateral drift per card. Move DOWN if the previous clip scrolled UP. BECAUSE jerky, hold-punctuated steps feel like events being processed. (M940)

WHEN panning a wide timeline -> run every part (sidebar, ruler, blocks) on ONE shared track. Peak ~126 px/frame mid-clip, ~2.9 frame widths total, long tail, no zoom. Fade blocks in at full width, never growing them. Clip with a fixed left gutter. BECAUSE a rigid track reads as camera, and growing bars read as charts. (M940)

WHEN a cursor must "click" -> glide it on an asymptotic curve (~85% of path in the first 0.7 s, then a 0.5 s creep), shrink it 15-20% as it approaches, hold 2 frames still. Press = target compresses ~23% (48 -> 37 px) or arrow to .75 over ~0.24 s, with no ring or flash. Trigger the response on the press-minimum frame. Exit by a fast curved sweep (7 frames, label tilts ~10°). BECAUSE the cause-effect gap of ~0 frames is what sells "real product". (M939, M942, M943)

WHEN expanding a card into a canvas -> animate as a camera zoom-OUT: container grows while its header content shrinks (scale 1 -> .39). Allow one overshoot (.63 -> 1.06 -> .82 of W). Children step in whole every 1-2 frames and are shrunk by the zoom, not by their own tweens. BECAUSE the viewer sees a zoom-out, so the content reads as spatial. (M939)

WHEN a chosen card carries state into a form (the M943 pattern) -> Collapse the card's SURFACE inward around the orb while the children keep size and are cropped by the shrinking rounded mask (10 frames). Shrink the siblings in place and fade them over ~0.16 s. Never slide siblings off. Meanwhile pull focus on the destination form by animating blur 4 -> 0 px over 0.46 s, not opacity. Fly the orb on a curved path: down, left, up, 0.8 s, d .22 W -> .036 W, 5 px blur at peak speed, no overshoot, landing in the form's slot. The destination label changes with the choice (a name -> a name). BECAUSE one continuous object makes the selection a traceable state change. (M942, M943)

WHEN a cursor must cross a scene to commit -> sweep an ARC (dip .23 H below its start, peak 80 px/frame), lean 20° clockwise at peak, one-sided 20-25 px smear, start 0.13 s after the dock lands. Keep it a single persistent arrow. Park it, blurred, in the layer behind between beats. BECAUSE persistence implies a person. (M943, M942)

WHEN switching to a close-up for a button press -> use ONE 50% double-exposed frame, then the 2.33x layout as a hard state. Scale the cursor less (1.5x). Glide in slowly for ~1 s. Press: 12% cursor shrink and 0.97 button scale for 0.1 s. Anticipate with a violet shadow growing to ~22 px. Burst 5 frames, width x2.2, blur 3 -> 25 px. Cut mid-burst. BECAUSE the viewer fills in the rest. (M943)

WHEN a product window arrives -> open from a slit (.10 W) with top and bottom edges fixed, content cropped and never stretched. Pause growth, then jump +.22 W in ONE frame. Slide panel and gallery up on two slightly different tracks (16 px smear at peak). Reveal sidebar rows top-down as the clip edge passes. Dock the logo disc to the sidebar slot concurrently (.10 -> .04 W, 20 px smear at peak). Reach rest by 1.4 s. BECAUSE the UI is staged (clip + rise) before it is read. (M944)

WHEN the hero beat is done and titles must take over -> tip the window back (y .11 -> .46, sides splay, lower half off-frame, 1.1 s), then drift only ~4 px for 2.3 s. Release the disc on an up-right arc (slow until 2.93, 65 px/frame peak at 3.03). Titles rise .06 H while alpha ramps linearly over 0.83 s; subtitle words stagger 3 frames. BECAUSE the foreground becomes a plinth and the headline gets clean space. (M944)

WHEN changing light/state colours -> use hard plateaus of 0.3-0.4 s with a 1-frame gap. Sync disc core, halo and window rim. Order white, teal, cyan, white. Never cross-fade. BECAUSE a hard step reads as a mode change. (M944)

WHEN ending a film on motion without a card -> accelerate a roll to -76° with smear on the UI (22/18 px) and sharp-ish titles (2 px, -20%). Never settle. BECAUSE the next shot takes over the momentum. (M944)

WHEN revealing a big number -> resolve it left to right from pixel squares and ASCII glyphs (final value from the first frame, a leading band 12-15 px). Scale it 96 -> 176 px while it resolves. Reach crisp in 0.7 s, hold ~0.47 s (it is one number), dissolve from both ends toward the centre in 0.33 s. Move the label plate DOWN, not up. BECAUSE it shows magnitude without a counter ticking. (M945)

WHEN gathering integrations around a product mark -> 9 upright tiles at 40° spacing, clockwise. Run the radius collapse fast (.63 -> .29 H in 8 frames) while the swirl decelerates 17 -> 10 -> 1°/frame. Bloat each tile 1.8x for ~4 frames in a wave that travels AGAINST the orbit, widening gaps 0.07 -> 0.27 s. Build the badge inside the orbit (disc .46 scale fading in, flame filling bottom-up from squares). Exit the tiles in a clockwise stagger (2-3 frames) with accelerating orbit. BECAUSE counter-rotation and the wave keep identity while the badge builds. (M945)

WHEN swapping an integration (carousel) -> move both candidates together (spacing .49 H), in steps with real holds: jump 0.12 H in 1 frame, hold 2, decelerate, hold 1. Keep the outgoing disc fading and shrinking (.9 -> .7x) while the incoming one scales .7 -> 1.0 and darkens 18% -> black. Break and re-link the connector by tint and bracket shape only (gray -> rust -> orange #CB4200, no glow or scale), and change it in ONE frame after the column rests (4.87 in M945). BECAUSE the link is the only thing that must feel "alive". (M945, M946)

WHEN closing on a logo -> make the preceding wipe a motif from the scene (the horn's white wave, stair-notched) and jerk the world left with accelerating offsets (-.04, -.10, -.29, -.41, -.63, -.86) with one repeated frame. Resolve the flame inside its silhouette (dots, then solid rising from the base, 0.6 s) and the word left to right with a solid front (~13 frames, paired frames). Let both drift ~.09 W left while resolving. Hold it 3.66 s with the flame tip swaying ±1% W (irregular ~1 s) and a static wordmark. End on the hold, no fade. BECAUSE the brand is "built" from the scene's own texture and the sway keeps a long hold alive. (M946)

WHEN a rolodex/stack opens a brand hook -> mirror two perspective stacks about the logo (outer sheets wider, top photos inverted), start them already on screen. Flip fast (0.1 s), advance slow (1.5 s), then spin clockwise as one rigid unit with rotation 2 -> 4 -> 11 -> 29 -> 74° and scale 1 -> 2.0 over 0.7 s with 10 px blur. Cut on frame while still big. BECAUSE the logo reads as the fixed centre that the whole moving machine revolves around. (M941)

WHEN a ring of photo cards orbits a headline -> use 10 upright cards of IRREGULAR size, tall ones further out. Enter by ease-out convergence (smear halves every ~0.15 s), then decelerate continuously (217 -> 75°/s), then fling outward 7x speed while the headline swells 1 -> 1.3. Let cards overlap the headline text and stay constant in size. Place the headline at vertical centre with word staggers of 5 frames. BECAUSE irregularity and overlap look photographed and not generated. (M941)

WHEN lighting a headline word by word -> each word starts .07 H low and grey (#B8B8B8, 1.5 px blur), rises over 0.67 s and goes black over 0.33 s. 5-frame stagger. BECAUSE reading order is locked and no word pops. (M941, M944)
WHEN typing a prompt in a demo -> reveal discrete prefixes at ~1 grapheme per frame with occasional 1-frame holds. No caret. About 1 s for 40 characters. BECAUSE it looks keyed, not animated. (M942)

WHEN defocusing background UI behind a hero -> blur it to ~4 px (copy still readable), hold, let the cursor blur with it, and never fade to grey. BECAUSE depth is carried by blur and readable copy stays on-screen. (M942, M943)

WHEN a spoken question or claim opens the piece -> DO put one word at a time on a near-empty page, 1-2 pose gaps apart (M947: 2,2,4,4 frames at 60 fps; M958: 0.27/0.16/0.17 s; M956: 0.06-0.10 s), each arriving oversized or offset and landing with strong ease-out, and RE-CENTRE the line each time (M947) or lay out final slots first and never re-centre (M956) -> BECAUSE arrival rhythm reads as speech, and the line is visibly still being formed. (M947, M956, M958)

WHEN a word is the first thing on screen -> DO start it 4-5x oversize and blurred (M947 "Ready" 0.39H -> 0.09H in 0.30 s; M953 red words 1.44x) so ~85% of the shrink happens in the first 8 frames and a 0.3-0.5 s tail finishes it -> BECAUSE it lands like a hit but does not bounce. Never overshoot. (M947, M953, M959)

WHEN type has to leave -> DO shrink it into the centre (0.55W -> 0.28W -> gone in 0.24 s), erase it with a centre-outward mask wipe, or scramble glyphs (+-12 deg -> 39 deg) and hard-switch; overlap the outgoing ghost under the incoming object for 2-4 frames. NEVER opacity-fade in place (the one fade, M958 1.63-1.90 at 90% -> 5%, is paired with outward push and badge growth, so it reads as being replaced by the icon). -> BECAUSE the eye keeps tracking an object instead of seeing a gap. (M947, M958)

WHEN the next object IS the continuation of the sentence -> DO open a gap in the line exactly the width of the incoming badge (M958: sides slide ~42 px / 0.06W fast-out, badge grows 0.04W -> 0.07W monotonic, second badge emerges from behind the first at 1.27) -> BECAUSE the icons stand in for words, so the line finishes as a pictogram; growth is monotonic, no 112% pop. (M958, M947 badge)

WHEN an object must change identity (two badges -> a cluster, a ring of letters -> a title) -> DO a ONE-FRAME hard switch plus a 5-frame recolour/shape settle (M958 1.90: muddy #69433C node -> red by 2.07; M947 3.10: scramble -> exactly 6 glyphs) and never draw in-between morph frames -> BECAUSE hard switches read as designed; gooey morphs read as generated. (M947, M958)

WHEN a letter ring or token ring is needed -> DO place items on an ellipse around the hero (M956: centre (0.52,0.62), radii 0.10W x 0.15H, upper tokens 0.03W / lower 0.06W as depth), 9 items entering 1-2 frames apart each at its own ring slot, flash bright (#fffaff core + glow) for ~0.13 s then settle to a plain fill, rotate clockwise 1-3 px/frame with glyphs staying upright, keep 1-2 tokens glowing -> BECAUSE the ring counts the inventory visibly and never reads as particle dust. (M956, M947)

WHEN an orbit/stroke accent is used -> DO enter it at maximum thickness (0.11H) from the corner, whip its head 0.8W in 0.10 s, thin it to 0.03H over 0.67 s, circle OUTSIDE the text, exit through the frame edge -> BECAUSE the stroke is a camera-like frame for the word and never competes with it. (M947)

WHEN a number must "resolve" -> DO roll through discrete values, one per frame, 15-23 steps in 0.5-0.9 s, step sizes decaying to ~0.07 at the end so it lands rather than stops (M954 $86.94 -> $100.00 in 16 frames; M958 2.71 -> 522.14 in 23 events) -> BECAUSE the viewer feels the amount arrive. Hero claims end on round values (100.00, 10% a name, 120+), product-data fields end on specific un-round values (522.14, 119 a name, 112/500) so the screen feels real. (M954, M955, M958)

WHEN a counter or percentage steps -> DO skip values (M955 skips 5%, M954 jumps 1.78/1.84/1.56 between 0.6-0.9 steps), hold 1-3 frames per value, and never tween digits -> BECAUSE uneven steps look measured; smooth rolls look like a compositing tool presets. (M954, M955, M958)

WHEN a number is the hero -> DO defocus only its edge glyphs (M954: "$" and final "0" blurred ~12 px, centre digits sharp until 1.07-1.20) and pull the view back 0.91W -> 0.63W in 0.20 s -> BECAUSE focus lands on the digits that carry the message. (M954)

WHEN a headline must hold for >1 s -> DO keep something else alive underneath (M955: a name +1/+2 every 1-3 frames for 1.87 s, mascot bob, blink at 1.07-1.27; M947/M953 text shrinks 9% over 0.6 s; M949 drifts at 1-30 px/step; never a frozen hold) -> BECAUSE a locked frame reads as slideware. (M947, M949, M953, M955)

WHEN a 3D phone/device is the hero -> DO crop it (top corners off-frame, bottom at y 0.97, screen ~0.39W), start at yaw -54 deg / x-tilt 29 / roll 11 and reach -9 / 24 / 2 in 6 held poses within 0.40 s under ~1870 px perspective, keep side thickness visible early (0.05W -> 0.01W), then drift; put the headline BEHIND the device and a big sparkle IN FRONT of its corner; UI is one perspective plane. Or fake 3D with stepped 2D camera jumps (M957: 0.13/0.20/0.23, 1.8x, dive via held steps) -> BECAUSE "a product you could hold" needs depth cues, not a flat rectangle. (M955, M957)

WHEN a screen is shown flat -> DO give it a camera: scale the window itself 0.70W -> 0.78W over 1.2 s (M953), never scale bars/cards separately; or pan the whole dark dashboard 0.33W left with 79% of it in 0.27 s and crop the left edge (M956); keep blurred secondary panels (7-15 px) -> BECAUSE parallax and focus tell the eye which panel is live. (M953, M956, M958)

WHEN a cursor enters -> DO make it oversized (M953 1.55-2.2x; M956 0.36W; M959 5.1x, mostly off-frame, blurred) and scale it about its TIP while it decelerates onto the target with 60% of the travel in the first frame step and a 0.5-0.9 s creep; never a hold before the click -> BECAUSE the cursor reads as thrown at the screen and the tip stays the anchor. (M953, M956, M959, M948)

WHEN a click happens -> DO a 2-3 frame press (cursor and target to 0.72-0.80 scale; M956 button -29% with arrow lagging one frame; M959 cursor -13% + tip down 0.03H), a hard colour step on the target, a bar dip of 15% recovering in 0.14 s, and a glow that decays over 0.3 s (peak 35 px blur @40% for M956); NEVER ripple rings or a white screen flash. For a hero CTA add one frame of label smear (95 px, 0.44W) and a swell of 1.02 -> BECAUSE the click is felt in the object, not announced by a graphic. (M953, M956, M959)

WHEN each of several cursors/agents appears -> DO give each ONE job and start them on different frames (M953: a name drags a card, a name recolours bars twice, a name clicks a heading; events every ~0.3 s from 1.94 to 2.74), name pills on each, cursors jump rather than interpolate across the cut -> BECAUSE "live collaboration" is shown as simultaneous cause and effect. (M953)

WHEN a prompt is typed -> DO type at human cadence (M949: 1.2 chars/step, 0.02-0.07 s inside words, 0.10 before an ending letter, 0.20 before a space, "le" together), 0.14H cap at large scale, a tall thin caret (0.008W x 0.25H) that never blinks and jumps on each glyph, a continuous leftward slide that accelerates 0.006W -> 0.027W per step, and snap scale by hard cut (x0.42) in the same frame the copy jumps ahead ("into one" appears at once). Keep the typo. For a UI field type 2-3 chars/frame with the newest 1-3 glyphs in the accent for 1 frame (M956) -> BECAUSE the viewer authors the sentence and the snap converts overflow into a committed, frame-fitting line. (M949, M956)

WHEN scale changes in a text beat -> DO hard-cut it (M949: 1.00 -> 0.42 -> 1.57x of large), not tween; and pair the cut with a content jump in the same frame -> BECAUSE a zoom interpolation announces itself; a snap is read as editing. Same for camera: M956 uses an accelerating ease-in push (2.80-3.44) then a DISCONTINUOUS jump to the macro (0.04W -> 0.27W). (M949, M956)

WHEN you need an end state / CTA -> DO stop on an object mid-motion that implies the viewer's next move: M959 shrinks button/bracket/cursor to 0.74/0.76/0.75 with the biggest step on the final frame and cuts to white before release; M949 ends 0.11 s into the send arrow's arrival, mid-slide, never showing the send; M958 ends with Buy pulsing and the camera still moving; M955 ends with the badge still shrinking on the last frame. -> BECAUSE the action transfers to the viewer. (M949, M955, M958, M959)

WHEN an icon/brand mark is the last thing -> DO cut hard to a flat ground (white/cream), start the mark at 1.5-1.9x, and settle it over 2.5 s with an exponential curve (1.864 -> 1.449 in 0.13 s -> 1.10 @2.4 -> 1.0 @4.0), no overshoot, no tagline, no fade; or a one-frame word card (M957 "Now", 0.10H, regular, left of centre at x 0.46, 3 px blur) as a chapter hand-off -> BECAUSE the settle is slow enough to feel alive and the single frame carries into the next scene. (M959, M957)

WHEN a title sits on its final slot -> DO set it OFF-CENTRE (x 0.47, y 0.50) with a gradient clipped to glyphs and add colour washes only at the end (lavender lower-left, cyan upper-right, centre white) -> BECAUSE an exact-centre title reads as default; the washes arrive with the resolve as the reward. (M947, M948)

WHEN a scene is a montage of styles -> DO strobe plates at 4 source frames (0.067 s) with a 2-frame first flash, 14 plates then repeats, hard cuts, zero fade, entering and exiting on hard cuts; the product glyph must not bloom into it (M948: glyph peaks at 0.30W x 0.46H and the cut lands on max growth velocity) -> BECAUSE a strobe at ~15 plates/s feels like range, and a bloom would soften the cut. (M948)

WHEN items are collected (M948 four references -> folder -> gallery) -> DO enter from four different edges on ~0.10 s staggers (one as a huge blurred foreground square 0.29 -> 0.39W), grab with a 0.03H lift (no halo), drag on a curved path while scaling 0.14 -> 0.09W, hide the stack in a glass folder, vanish the folder on a single frame, then spring the result (card 0.31H -> 0.58H, thumbnails on 2-frame staggers with 0.06H overshoot) -> BECAUSE overshoot saved for one payoff moment reads as reward; everywhere else decelerate with no bounce. (M948)

WHEN objects are consumed (M954 monster) -> DO shrink them toward the mouth 6-10 frames with rotation (+5 -> +18 deg) and darkening, grow the mouth over them rather than flying them in, show eyes/teeth without a pop, keep pupils the same colour as the head, and push in to 0.80W then pull back (never end on black) -> BECAUSE character beats come from flat shapes with deliberate asymmetry, not 3D polish. (M954)

WHEN a world changes (new product, new ground) -> DO hard-cut and carry ONE literal object, word, caret, or UI across (M947->M948 title + washes + banana at (0.70, 0.50); M948->M949 gray caret centre; M957->M958 "Now"; M958->M959 the last terminal frame held 1 frame) -> BECAUSE a film of 15 different looks still reads as one piece. (M947-M949, M957-M959)

WHEN stepping motion (the "on twos" look) -> DO hold every pose 2 source frames and place all onsets on those steps; keep the step across typing, translation, scale and stroke. Only the non-step exceptions are product surfaces (camera moves in M953/M958 are smooth at 30 fps) -> BECAUSE a consistent frame rhythm across the film is what makes it feel hand-animated rather than interpolated. (M947, M948, M949)

WHEN a hard cut hides a camera: land it at maximum velocity or just before a hold (M948 1.23 mid-swell; M954 2.07 after scan fade 0.73/0.50/0.30/0.13; M958 3.04 with the circle at 0.25W and cream right; M959 1.53 on the largest shrink step) -> BECAUSE motion continues in the viewer's head across the cut.

WHEN a state change should read as "engineered" and not "animated" -> DO a hard cut on an exact frame into ~90% of the final state, then a 3-10% ease-out settle over 7-14 frames (disc r108 -> r120 in 0.5 s; 3 rings .48 -> .45; 13 rings drift +3% R; tangent bars +66% in 7 frames; dial arcs decay x0.57/frame) BECAUSE the cut gives impact and the tiny settle gives life without a morph. (M962)

WHEN a sequence of diagrams/CAD states cuts on a beat -> DO a constant cut interval (10 frames = 0.333 s at 30 fps for four consecutive cuts), each state complete at the cut (dashes full length, labels present) with only nodes/handles arriving 1-3 frames later in two waves (even ticks +1 frame, odd +2) BECAUSE the viewer reads cut = beat and detail as an echo. (M962)

WHEN you need a through-line object -> DO make one object (a 22 px dot, 3.1% H) the carrier: it rides the end of the typed line, steps through every state, and in the next moment IS the seed of the product shape; end the moment with it displaced (x 0.28) so the next opens at that position (0.27) BECAUSE a continuous object makes two edits feel like one film. (M962 -> M963)

WHEN text types in -> DO keep the typed line centred and move any carrier (dot, caret, emblem) with its live right edge on every event (dot +0.1 W across 18 chars, even on space steps) BECAUSE it reads as composing now, and nothing is anchored to a fixed spot. (M962, M969)

WHEN typing copy -> DO use an authored rhythm: bursts of 1-frame (or 2-frame at 15 fps) letters, 6-10 frame pauses after spaces ("This " held 10 frames, "This is " held 6), skipped intermediate states ("Th" never shown, "my" arrives as 2 letters, "l" never alone before "le"), and a slower last word (letters every 3 frames after fast whole words) BECAUSE metronomic one-char-per-frame typing is the clearest slop tell. (M962, M965, M966, M969)

WHEN removing a line -> DO wipe it (a clip edge sweeping through the glyphs while the line slides the same direction, 5 frames, accelerating) or vanish words in hard steps 2 frames apart; use per-letter backspace only when erasing is part of the story (brand name erased as petals swirl into a mark) BECAUSE mid-glyph cuts feel physical. (M962, M964, M968)

WHEN words arrive in a headline -> DO pop each word whole on one frame (no fade, no blur, no typing), offset ~0.04 H low or 16 px to the entry side, decay x0.6-0.72 per frame (90% in 5 frames at 24 fps), no overshoot, and slide the whole line so the group stays centred BECAUSE the viewer reads one beat per word and the line is never off-balance. (M964, M967)

WHEN a new word arrives and needs attention -> DO give it the ONE accent for the shortest time that registers (24 fps: 1-2 frames in cycling flash colours; 30 fps: 6 frames purple; 60 fps: 0.28 s linear violet -> ink) and settle to ink BECAUSE colour = "this is arriving", and the frame stays monochrome at rest. (M966, M967, M973, M974)

WHEN spending a colour budget -> DO keep text/ink and ground monochrome and spend colour on (a) arrival, (b) the payoff of the whole film (M963 gets its only colour in the last demo, 0.9 s, sparse ~5% orange), (c) block/brand marks BECAUSE colour used once reads as an event. (M963, M964, M967)

WHEN picking a film clock -> DO choose one and hold it for the whole moment: 2-frame holds on even frames (15 fps look) for indie/technical sets (M967-M969), 24 fps with smooth moves + stepped reveals for a product-explainer (M964-M966), 30 fps for CAD idents (M962/963), 60 fps smooth for brand-morph and UI zoom (M973/974) BECAUSE mixed step rates look like a bug. (M962-M974)

WHEN two scales must be shown (cluster -> close-up -> ribbon) -> DO hard-cut in ONE frame (0.037 W -> 0.136 W = 3.7x; then back to 0.035 W) and let the background keep its own scale and drift (tiles 73 px pitch, 0.07 W/s left) BECAUSE a cut says "different distance", a zoom says "camera", and the background not scaling keeps the world stable. (M964)

WHEN dissolving a field into a logo or screen -> DO use real hard-edged cells (1.5-2.5% W) with stepped coverage (90% -> 60% -> 35% -> 10% -> 0 over 0.33 s, opening from the bottom; or 12x12 -> 15x15 -> 17x17 -> 20x20 grid retreating to corners in 3 steps over 0.27 s), never opacity BECAUSE pixel occlusion reads as digital craft and the cells carry the brand colour. (M965, M968)

WHEN revealing a logo -> DO enter oversized and blurred and scale DOWN (0.28 W -> 0.10 W, blur 18 -> 0 px, halving the excess every 2 frames, 0.33 s), or hold full at frame 0 and shrink with exponential ease-out (scaleX 1.46 -> 1.0 in 8 frames, creep to 0.96, then accelerate and cut on one frame); never scale up from zero or fade BECAUSE "arrives from the camera" reads as authority. (M968, M965)

WHEN transforming one identity into another -> DO flip per glyph left to right at ~2 frames (60 fps) per glyph: old glyph squashes up to a hairline (3 frames), new grows from a baseline hairline in 6-8 frames, two thin strokes visible at different heights; fixed left anchor (x 0.49) so the eye never travels; add an anticipation spread (+26% tracking over 0.19 s) before the second flip BECAUSE the viewer sees both names from one lockup. (M973)

WHEN swapping icons -> DO spin the old one up (accelerating to ~30 deg/frame while shrinking to 0.87x), cross-dissolve over 8 frames on a shared centre, and let the new one inherit the spin (-139 deg decelerating to 0 over 0.26 s) with one 4% overshoot at 0.87 s BECAUSE conserved momentum makes a dissolve feel like one object changing. (M973)

WHEN diving from the brand into the product -> DO scale the camera from frame 0 with no hold at a constant octave rate (1 -> 21.9 in 0.53 s, ~x1.5-2 per 0.067 s), translate toward a feature of the logo (the underscore) not the centre, so it exits the frame edge, let the feature become a near-full-frame white mass, fade the mass in place in 3 frames, show 3 blank frames, then zoom a larger container out to rest (0.05/0.98 -> 0.25/0.78 in 0.62 s, stroke 10 -> 4 px) BECAUSE the logo is felt to contain the product. (M974)

WHEN a UI line is longer than the box -> DO make the container wider than the frame (1.78 W), type per glyph with a +25 -> -24 -> 0 px wave (0.035 H, 14-frame life, colour violet -> ink in 17 frames), and pan the whole UI as one group (eased, peak mid-typing) so controls arrive by the pan, never a pop BECAUSE the type has liveliness without a cursor or wrap and the pan "reveals" the action. (M974)

WHEN showing a cursor in a prompt UI -> DO bring it in late (0.7 s before the end of typing), move it in 2-frame steps with decay x0.72, bending toward vertical, park it before the action, no hover/press/ripple; show the click as the next container replacing the bar at full size on a ground that shifts one step darker/greyer (#ECEBE3 -> #C4C2B1) BECAUSE the cut is the proof and nothing wastes a frame. (M969)

WHEN a button must react -> DO cross-colour it: disc black -> #969696 -> white while the arrow goes white -> same grey (invisible at the midpoint) -> black, 0.28 s, no scale BECAUSE it reads "sent" without a cartoon press. (M974)

WHEN demonstrating a parameter system -> DO use a fixed lattice where nothing moves except per-dot size, opacity or colour, driven by a spatial function (radial wave 20 px/frame, row band, ring, left/right sweep, radial colour front at ring n start 6.10 + 0.085n s), 0.8-0.9 s per demo, amplitudes escalating per repetition (6.6/7.7/8.4 px), base 4.7 px vs large 13.3 px BECAUSE the viewer infers a system with knobs from one object. (M963)

WHEN labelling the active parameter -> DO scroll the whole list one line (20 px = line height) behind a FIXED bullet in 0.33 s with a snap (53% of travel in one frame, 93% in four), dip the bullet 13 -> 9 -> 13.8 px on the same beat, change the word colour only (#A3A3A3 <-> #000, never weight) BECAUSE the fixed anchor keeps the reader's eye in place. (M963)

WHEN a title must feel like an act break -> DO squeeze the old act with ease-in (scale 0.98 -> 0.91 -> 0.74 -> 0.30 in 4 steps), jitter 6 px strips +-1 px for 0.4 s, hard cut, then resolve the new, bigger type word by word (0.11 H -> 0.16 H), each from 0.73 scale in the accent to 1.0 white in ~0.2 s BECAUSE the anticipation + size jump make the cut an event. (M967)

WHEN a reel of categories flips -> DO swap card + badge together on a syncopated 4/2-frame pattern (13 swaps in 1.4 s), no crossfade, same container scale track (0.30 -> 1.0 over 0.8 s ease-out), the outer words creep apart behind it BECAUSE the viewer reads "many" without reading each. (M967)

WHEN ending a moment -> DO end mid-motion (phrases still sliding, man still rising, badge still turning, dial half-exited), or on a one-frame new element (capsule, card, 8-block grid + green bar) BECAUSE the next moment picks up the momentum and the last frame matches the first frame of the next. (M962, M963, M965, M966, M969, M973, M974)

WHEN holding for the payoff -> DO hold only after the payoff lands (lockup 0.67 s static, headline 0.67 s with a solid caret) and keep micro-drift everywhere else (tile drift 0.07 W/s, creeping word spread to 0.14 W, orb breathing 0.255 -> 0.26 W, 0.4% shrink steps) BECAUSE nothing freezes except what must be read. (M964, M966, M967, M968, M969)

WHEN text onsets are synced -> DO land each onset on the spoken word (M967 voice 0.13-3.83 s, words at 0.07/0.33/0.47, then 2.33/2.47/2.67) and spread the gaps to the speech (4, 6 frames) BECAUSE the viewer hears the headline as a list. (M964, M967, M968)

WHEN scaling type by role -> DO use technical annotation 1.3% H (9 px), ident title 4.4% H (32 px), phrase 5-6.4% H, menu 2.4% H, UI prompt 4% H, act-one word 11% H, act-two word 16% H, brand word 21% H (154 px); weights 400-650, never bold, tracking -0.4 px at small sizes to -6 px at 154 px BECAUSE role-based scale gives hierarchy without bold. (M962-M969)

WHEN a camera/parallax pan is needed -> DO use two pushes with different accelerations (fast-then-slow, then accelerate to a peak 0.025 W/frame and settle) and 2-2.4x parallax between layers (tiles > diagram > orb), exits clipped by the frame edge, staggered (text 1.54 s, grid 1.92 s), never one ease BECAUSE a single ease looks like a keyframe, two pushes look like a camera operator. (M966)

WHEN you need a generative texture -> DO use flat, hard squares on a grid (73 px or 14.6 px pitch, 3-14 px cells, #2D2121 on #1E1212, clusters with holes) born in place and never moving or flickering, delayed 0.2 s after the headline lands BECAUSE texture without competition. (M964, M967)

WHEN a container replaces a screen -> DO contract the old container with ease-in (0.70 -> 0.64 W, -9%) then replace it outright with the next container at full size (0.83 x 0.85) and a faint halo; a 1-frame empty capsule/card is a placeholder for the next scene BECAUSE it sets up the next moment. (M966, M969)
